```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Query BigQuery with each visitor's Google account. The client returns data
frames and handles waiting for query jobs and fetching result pages; you
don't need bigrquery or an ODBC driver.

## Google Cloud setup

Create a [Web OAuth client](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server)
in Google Cloud, configure its consent screen, and register
`http://localhost:8100` as the redirect URI. Enable the BigQuery API for the
query project. Users need permission to create query jobs in that project
and to read any data they query.

Put your registration's values in a local `.Renviron` file and restart R:

```text
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID=your-client-id
OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret
```

The `project` below runs and pays for queries. Set `location` to match
your datasets when querying data; the example uses `"EU"`.

## A complete app

Save this as `app.R` and replace the example connection settings:

```{r app}
library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

client <- oauth_db_bigquery_client(
  client_id = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_ID"),
  client_secret = Sys.getenv("OAUTHDB_CLIENT_SECRET"),
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:8100"
)

ui <- oauth_ui(fluidPage(
  actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
  actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
  tableOutput("rows")
), id = "auth", client = client)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  bigquery <- oauth_db_bigquery_api(
    auth$connection,
    project = "billing-project",
    location = "EU"
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    bigquery$query("SELECT SESSION_USER() AS signed_in_user")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(port = 8100), uiPattern = ".*")
```

Run `shiny::runApp(port = 8100)` in that directory, then open
`http://localhost:8100` and sign in. The output waits for sign-in and clears
when you sign out.

The first query shows the signed-in Google identity. Replace it with
GoogleSQL for your data, using `project.dataset.table` names when the data
belongs to a different project.

## Query with parameters

Use named parameters for values entered by a visitor. This example assumes
a `reporting.Orders` table with a `country` column:

```{r parameters}
output$rows <- renderTable({
  bigquery$query(
    "SELECT * FROM reporting.Orders WHERE country = @country LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list(country = "NL"),
    maximum_bytes_billed = "1000000000"
  )
})
```

`maximum_bytes_billed` limits the bytes a query may bill. A row limit on
its own doesn't provide that limit.

## Browse datasets and tables

These methods return dataset or table IDs. Call them inside a render or
reactive expression:

```{r browse}
output$datasets <- renderPrint(bigquery$datasets())
output$tables <- renderPrint(bigquery$tables("reporting"))
```

Add `verbatimTextOutput("datasets")` and `verbatimTextOutput("tables")` to
the UI if you use these outputs. Set `dataset = "reporting"` when creating
the client to use it as the default dataset for unqualified table names.

## Results and longer queries

INT64 and decimal values remain strings to preserve precision. Dates become
`Date`, timestamps become UTC `POSIXct`, and nested or repeated fields use
list columns. Use `raw = TRUE` to inspect the REST result and schema;
`?oauth_db_bigquery_api` describes parameter types and other options.

Queries run synchronously and collect their results in R memory. A timeout
or sign-out stops fetching results but doesn't cancel a submitted BigQuery
job. Each request obtains a current token for the authorization that started
the query. For stored results or background work, see
[Authentication and sessions](authorization.html).
